title: Association of Multidisciplinary Care Team Engagement With Hemoglobin A<sub>1c</sub> Among Medicaid Enrollees With Diabetes: A Doubly Robust Machine Learning Analysis
summary: In a retrospective Virginia Medicaid cohort, doubly robust machine-learning analysis estimated that multidisciplinary care-team engagement was associated with a 0.30 percentage-point lower follow-up HbA1c (95% CI −0.58 to −0.01), with larger estimated reductions at higher baseline HbA1c. The observational analysis does not prove a causal treatment effect.
ai_technology: Doubly robust debiased machine learning estimates the engagement association and generalized random forests characterize treatment-effect heterogeneity.
organization: Waymark, San Francisco, CA; University of California, San Francisco, San Francisco, CA; Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York, NY; Virginia Commonwealth University, Richmond, VA

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; publication date and first result-bearing version checked.

evidence.tested: The article used doubly robust debiased machine learning and generalized random forests with sensitivity analyses in a retrospective Medicaid cohort.
evidence.unknown: Association from observational data; unmeasured confounding and selection cannot be excluded.
evidence.ai_role: Doubly robust debiased machine learning estimates the engagement association and generalized random forests characterize treatment-effect heterogeneity.
